business_problem: BAEMIN needed a lightweight but scalable platform for a new country launch that could handle spiky food-delivery demand without burdening a seven-person team.
solution_summary: Woowa Brothers Vietnam built BAEMIN's local food-delivery platform on MongoDB Atlas running on AWS so a small team could launch quickly without operating its own database estate. Atlas stores the order, rider, and operational data behind recommendation logic that selects riders, determines routes, and keeps deliveries fast, while also exposing infrastructure metrics for monitoring and tuning. Because the service experiences sharp traffic peaks around meal times and weekends, the managed platform's elasticity and operational tooling were especially important for the seven-person team. That design helped BAEMIN expand from three cities to 21, improve customer satisfaction, and become one of Vietnam's leading food-delivery apps.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores delivery, rider, and operational data for BAEMIN's Vietnam platform.

data_flow: Order, rider, and operational data flows into MongoDB Atlas on AWS, where BAEMIN's delivery systems, recommendation logic, and monitoring metrics can scale up and down with meal-time traffic spikes.
business_outcome: BAEMIN expanded rapidly across Vietnam, handled spiky food-delivery demand, and became a top market app with broad geographic coverage and strong customer satisfaction.
metrics: The first version of BAEMIN was developed within six months.
In 2021, it expanded from serving three cities to serving 21 cities throughout Vietnam, representing a 70% increase in the number of customers.
It also increased its employee numbers in Vietnam by 40% in 2021.
architecture_clues: MongoDB Atlas runs on AWS and exposes practical metrics for effective system analysis.
The platform must absorb large traffic spikes around mealtimes and weekends.
The local rollout used a new stack rather than the full ten-year Korean platform.
